response.consequence: If a calendar service fails to construct or load during a reschedule, the error is not logged. It surfaces as an unhandled rejection, which can crash the process on newer Node versions. The deletion also races with the response because it is not awaited.
response.explanation: The callback is now `async` and awaits getCalendar, but forEach neither awaits it nor propagates its rejection. Before the change, a synchronous throw from getCalendar (for example a CalendarService constructor error) was caught by the surrounding try/catch and logged. Now that error becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the catch block never runs. The same applies to the identical code in vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, and to the bookings.tsx reschedule handler, which has no try/catch.

other_findings.consequence: Cold start and bundle load are no better than the old static imports, and every app module is loaded in every importing context. A failed import also becomes an eagerly created rejected promise that is only handled when a caller awaits that key.
other_findings.explanation: Each property in the appStore object literal calls `import(...)` as the object is built. All ~30 app modules therefore start loading as soon as app-store/index is first imported, whether or not they are used. Lazy loading would need functions such as `() => import(...)`, with callers invoking them. Nothing else changes, because callers simply await the property.
other_findings.title: appStore dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module load

response.title: try/catch no longer covers calendar deletion after making forEach callback async

response.explanation: The change adds `await` to the `appStore[...]` lookup. I did not open `appStore` to confirm its shape. The existing check `"lib" in paymentApp` assumes a resolved module object. The added `await` fits that check, and it also works if the entries are plain objects. Without it, a lazily imported entry would be a Promise and the check would always fail. I found no input or state where the change goes wrong.
response.title: No defect found in the added await

response.consequence: When an attendee cancels all remaining recurring bookings, the external calendar events may not be deleted before the handler responds. Deletion failures go unreported. The events can remain on the external calendars.
response.explanation: In handleCancelBooking, the recurring-event branch iterates the calendar credentials with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. forEach does not wait for async callbacks. The change adds `await getCalendar`, so each callback now suspends before it deletes anything or pushes to `apiDeletes`. The surrounding handler can reach its `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` before any deletion has finished or been recorded. A rejection from `deleteEvent` inside the callback also becomes an unhandled rejection. The sibling branch the change did convert to a `for...of` loop awaits correctly. This one was left as `forEach`.
response.title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions run in an un-awaited async forEach
